9. "OBBB cuts Medicare."

Fact: It doesn’t touch a dime of Medicare benefits. Not a single cut to welfare programs.

10. "People will die — millions will be kicked off healthcare."

Fact: OBBB protects coverage for those who qualify. It ends fraud, abuse, and illegal access—freeing up resources for those in real need.

11. "OBBB will hurt people with disabilities."

Fact: It protects and strengthens Medicaid for Americans with disabilities — no loss or change in coverage.

12. "This punishes vulnerable Americans with work requirements."

Fact: Requirements only apply to able-bodied adults without young kids — promoting dignity, stability, and health.

Claim 4: "Hospitals will close as a result of Medicaid cuts and providers will be harmed."

Reality: Republicans are investing a record $50 billion in new funding going to safety net hospitals, while also eliminating financing scams that risked the long-term sustainability of the Medicaid program. 

For years states and providers have relied on gimmicks to draw down excessive federal funds to pay for other non-Medicaid state expenses. 

President Biden allowed these abuses to explode over the last four years, setting Medicaid on an unsustainable path. H.R. 1 fixes these abuses while still making investments to support the health care providers that need it, along with preserving the ability of states to invest in their hospitals without relying on such gimmicks.

This bill doubles down on Republicans’ commitments to our providers. The bill establishes the Rural Health Transformation Program, which directly invests $50 billion to improve health care in rural and underserved communities. 

Additionally, the bill provides certainty for doctors by boosting their reimbursement and allows for larger future payment updates.

Claim 6: "Work requirements don’t work – they’re too burdensome for states and can’t be implemented."

Reality: Able-bodied adults or co-occurring exclusions should work to receive taxpayer-subsidized Medicaid coverage. A new study from the American Enterprise Institute found that able-bodied, unemployed adult Medicaid recipients without dependents average 6.1 hours a day — 184 hours a month — watching television and socializing. 

These individuals spend less than a combined one hour a day looking for work or caring for others. That figure is 50% higher than for employed beneficiaries. 

On top of that, Republicans learned from state experiences and have applied those lessons to this bill, in order to such as not be overly burdensome for states and enrollees.
Republicans remain committed to putting American beneficiaries first by limiting coverage to just U.S. citizens and certain non-permanent residents like green-card holders.
